soil-env-102.caption: The carbon cycle is divided into five reservoirs.

soil-env-106.caption: Soil organic carbon is the largest of these land carbon stores.

soil-env-108.caption: Most upland topsoils fall in a narrow band of organic carbon content.

soil-env-154.caption: Carbon moves into permafrost by burial and leaves it mainly by microbial respiration.
soil-env-154.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Plants] --> B[Soil carbon]
B -->|burial, cryogenic processes| C[Permafrost carbon]
C -->|microbial respiration| D[Air: CO2, methane]
D --> A
C -.-> E[Ocean, wider cycle]

soil-env-146.caption: The active layer thaws each summer above the year-round frozen permafrost.
layers: Thaws in summer, freezes in autumn; roots here

soil-env-103.caption: The fast and slow carbon cycles differ in route and timescale.

soil-env-130.caption: Permafrost zones are defined by the share of land underlain by permafrost.

soil-env-114.caption: Warming speeds soil respiration, releasing carbon that adds to warming.

soil-env-140.caption: Thaw releases carbon gases that warm the climate and drive more thaw.

soil-env-126.caption: Silicate weathering moves CO2 from the air into ocean carbonate.
soil-env-126.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Atmospheric CO2] -->|rain, groundwater| B[Carbonic acid]
B -->|dissolves silicates| C[Dissolved bicarbonate]
C -->|soil, groundwater| D[Ocean]
D -->|organisms| E[Carbonate shells]

soil-env-067.caption: Degradation classes are set by how much yield potential is lost.

soil-env-077.caption: Drylands cover two-thirds of Africa but much less of other regions.

soil-env-072.caption: Losing vegetation sets off the chain that turns fertile land into hardpan.
soil-env-072.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Drought, overgrazing, tillage, deforestation] --> B[Most vegetation lost]
B --> C[Dry topsoil unprotected]
C -->|wind, flash floods| D[Topsoil removed]
D --> E[Infertile lower layers bake]
E --> F[Unproductive hardpan]

soil-env-078.caption: Desertification feeds dust storms, and dust can in turn worsen desertification.

soil-env-098.caption: Grassland degrades through three stages toward bare black soil.
soil-env-098.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Light: scattered dead patches] --> B[Moderate: patches grow, pests]
B --> C[High: vast dead grass]
C -.->|severe| D[Heitutan: bare black soil]

soil-env-186.caption: The four forms of soil degradation each harm the soil in a different way.
rows: Soil displaced by water or wind

soil-env-020.caption: Excess nutrients lead from algal blooms to oxygen loss and dead fish.
soil-env-020.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Excess nutrients] --> B[Algal bloom]
B --> C[Bottom plants shaded out]
B -->|algae die| D[Bacteria decompose them]
D --> E[Oxygen used up]
E --> F[Fish, invertebrates die]

soil-env-013.caption: Risk assessment moves from a qualitative model to detailed quantitative study.
soil-env-013.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Site suspected of contamination] --> B[Desk study, site walkover]
B --> C[Conceptual site model]
C --> D[Generic quantitative assessment]
D -->|screening value exceeded| E[Detailed quantitative assessment]

soil-env-268.caption: Typical upper background levels differ widely between elements.

soil-hist-119.caption: Each radiometric method covers a different span of ages and kinds of sample.
rows: A few years to about 700,000 years

soil-hist-124.caption: Luminescence dating reads the charge grains gather after burial resets them.
soil-hist-124.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Daylight bleaches grains] --> B[Grains buried]
B -->|natural radiation| C[Trapped charge builds up]
C -->|stimulate with light or heat| D[Luminescence signal]
D --> E[Burial age]

soil-hist-079.caption: Micrometeorite impacts make agglutinates and nanophase iron, which darken and redden lunar soil.
soil-hist-079.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Micrometeorite impacts] -->|melt| B[Agglutinates]
A -->|vaporize| C[Nanophase iron]
B --> F[Soil darker, redder]
C --> F

soil-hist-137.caption: Viking's control test separated chemistry from biology by heat-sterilizing a duplicate.
soil-hist-137.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Positive result] --> B[Heat-sterilize duplicate sample]
B --> C{Activity persists?}
C -->|yes| D[Chemistry]
C -->|no| E[Biology]
